title: Adjectives III: Word Formation
description: Use prefixes, suffixes and sentence clues to form the right adjective.
objectives: Use meaning and grammar to choose the form

source.title: Advanced Grammar & Vocabulary — Express Publishing
source.note: Lesson explanations, examples and practice have been adapted for independent study from the supplied unit. Answers and explanations are editorial, not a publisher answer key.

lessons.title: Start with the sentence
lessons.body: Identify the required word class. A gap before a noun often needs an adjective. A gap after a linking verb can also need an adjective. Then check whether the meaning must be positive or negative.

lessons.title: Negative prefixes
lessons.body: English uses several negative prefixes: un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis- and ab-. Learn each full word; the choice is not always predictable. In- often becomes im- before p or m, il- before l and ir- before r.

lessons.title: Adjective suffixes
lessons.body: Suffixes can change a noun or verb into an adjective. Common patterns include -ive, -able, -ible, -ic, -ial, -less and -ish. Spelling sometimes changes.

lessons.title: Watch meaning, not just spelling
lessons.body: Related forms may have different meanings. Arguable means open to debate or capable of being argued; argumentative describes someone who argues. Economic relates to the economy; economical means using resources carefully.
examples: an arguable claim; an argumentative person
an economic crisis; an economical car

lessons.title: Check the finished answer
lessons.body: Read the whole sentence again. Check spelling, meaning, agreement and the collocation. Do not add a negative prefix unless the context requires it.
examples: The text is too blurred to read: illegible.

vocabulary.definition: Easy to reach, enter or use.
vocabulary.example: The library is accessible to wheelchair users.
She sounded apologetic about the delay.

vocabulary.definition: Open to debate, or possible to argue.
vocabulary.example: It is arguable that the policy helped.

vocabulary.definition: Able to make firm decisions promptly.
Careful not to embarrass others or reveal private information.
vocabulary.example: Please be discreet about the news.

vocabulary.definition: Doing what you are told to do.
Believable or reasonably likely to be true.
vocabulary.example: That sounds like a plausible explanation.

vocabulary.definition: Sensible and likely to work in real situations.
Giving someone an advantage over others.
vocabulary.example: Relatives should not receive preferential treatment.

vocabulary.note: opposite: irreplaceable; not identical to disposable.

vocabulary.definition: Fully developed and ready to eat.
Very careful to act honestly and fairly.
vocabulary.example: He is scrupulous about declaring expenses.

exerciseGroups.title: Form the adjective
exerciseGroups.instruction: Use the capitalised word to form an adjective that fits.

questions.explanation: Preferential treatment means a special advantage.

questions.prompt: Stop behaving like a small child; it is ___. (CHILD)
questions.explanation: Childish criticises immature behaviour.

questions.prompt: The programme taught me a great deal; it was ___. (INFORMATION)
questions.explanation: Informative means giving useful information.

questions.prompt: The country faces a serious ___ crisis. (ECONOMY)
questions.explanation: Economic relates to the economy; economical means resource-saving.

questions.prompt: He disagrees with everything and is very ___. (ARGUE)
questions.explanation: Argumentative describes someone inclined to argue.
Deceptive is the usual adjective here.
The resignation indicates dissatisfaction, requiring a negative form.

questions.prompt: For some ___ reason, she left without a word. (EXPLAIN)
questions.explanation: Inexplicable means impossible to explain; unexplained means no explanation has been given.

questions.prompt: The judges found no faults: a ___ performance. (FLAW)
questions.explanation: The suffix -less means without.

questions.prompt: Too many ___ nights left him exhausted. (SLEEP)
questions.explanation: Sleepless means without sleep.

questions.prompt: She can talk anyone into anything; she is ___. (PERSUADE)
questions.explanation: Persuasive means good at convincing others.

questions.prompt: He was very ___ about missing the appointment. (APOLOGISE)
questions.explanation: Apologetic means showing regret.

exerciseGroups.title: Education in context
exerciseGroups.instruction: Build an adjective from the word in capitals.

questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is educational. Check how it fits the sentence.
The appropriate adjective is competitive. Check how it fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: Students need to be well-informed and ___. (KNOW)
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is knowledgeable. Check how it fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: It is ___ that one approach suits everyone. (ARGUE)
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is arguable. Check how it fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: A ___ classroom is not the only place to learn. (TRADITION)
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is traditional. Check how it fits the sentence.
The appropriate adjective is impossible. Check how it fits the sentence.
The appropriate adjective is excessive. Check how it fits the sentence.
The appropriate adjective is beneficial. Check how it fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: A focused study session is more ___. (PRODUCE)
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is productive. Check how it fits the sentence.
The appropriate adjective is irresistible. Check how it fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: For some tasks, a teacher may be ___ to a machine. (PREFER)
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective is preferable. Check how it fits the sentence.

exerciseGroups.title: Vocabulary recall
exerciseGroups.instruction: Choose the word or phrase that matches the meaning.

questions.prompt: Easy to reach, enter or use.
questions.explanation: The library is accessible to wheelchair users. accessibility; opposite: inaccessible.
The measurements are accurate. accuracy; opposite: inaccurate.
She sounded apologetic about the delay. Related to apologise/apologize and apology.

questions.prompt: Open to debate, or possible to argue.
questions.explanation: It is arguable that the policy helped. Different from argumentative.
He becomes argumentative when tired. Describes behaviour.
She gave a coherent account. coherence; opposite: incoherent.

questions.prompt: Able to make firm decisions promptly.
questions.explanation: We need a decisive leader. decisiveness; opposite: indecisive.

questions.prompt: Careful not to embarrass others or reveal private information.
questions.explanation: Please be discreet about the news. discretion; opposite: indiscreet. Not discrete (separate).
The fee seems excessive. From excess; excessive exposure.
He is knowledgeable about birds. From knowledge.
Please make your handwriting legible. legibility; opposite: illegible.
There is a logical explanation. logic; opposite: illogical.
She remained a loyal friend. loyalty; opposite: disloyal.
Service has returned to normal. normality; opposite: abnormal.

questions.prompt: Doing what you are told to do.
questions.explanation: The dog is very obedient. obedience; opposite: disobedient.
Wait for the official announcement. opposite: unofficial.
His approach is orthodox. orthodoxy; opposite: unorthodox.

questions.prompt: Believable or reasonably likely to be true.
questions.explanation: That sounds like a plausible explanation. plausibility; opposite: implausible.
It was a polite request. politeness; opposite: impolite.

questions.prompt: Sensible and likely to work in real situations.
questions.explanation: We need a practical solution. practicality; opposite: impractical.
Give me the precise location. precision; opposite: imprecise.

questions.prompt: Giving someone an advantage over others.
questions.explanation: Relatives should not receive preferential treatment. From prefer; common: preferential treatment.
The damaged part is replaceable. opposite: irreplaceable; not identical to disposable.
She is a responsible employee. responsibility; opposite: irresponsible.

questions.prompt: Fully developed and ready to eat.
questions.explanation: These pears are ripe. ripeness; opposite: unripe.

questions.prompt: Very careful to act honestly and fairly.
questions.explanation: He is scrupulous about declaring expenses. scruples; opposite: unscrupulous.
